为什么"产卵场"的连通性，往往决定禁渔能不能真正见效？

Why does spawning-ground connectivity often decide whether a fishing ban really works?

鱼需要洄游到特定浅滩或支流产卵，如果大坝、堤岸把通道切断，就算不禁渔鱼也"生不出"；保护产卵场和洄游通道，比单纯禁捕更治本。
Fish migrate to specific shallows or tributaries to spawn; if dams and banks cut the path, stocks can't breed even without fishing. Protecting spawning grounds and migration routes is more fundamental than the ban alone.

禁渔之后，江豚为什么被当作长江健康的"晴雨表"？

After the ban, why is the finless porpoise a "barometer" of Yangtze health?

江豚处在食物链上层、对水质和饵料鱼敏感，它的数量回升说明整条江的饵料、水质和连通性都在变好，是生态系统复苏的信号。
As an upper-food-chain animal sensitive to water quality and prey fish, a rising porpoise count signals better prey, water and connectivity—a sign the whole river is healing.

长江"十年禁渔"为什么是"十年"而不是更短？

Why is the Yangtze fishing ban set at "ten years" rather than less?

许多鱼类的性成熟和种群恢复需要多个繁殖周期，十年约等于覆盖几代鱼的生命史，让种群有足够时间回弹，短了往往"刚恢复又被捕"。
Many fish need several spawning cycles to recover; ten years spans a few fish generations, giving stocks time to rebound—shorter bans often cut recovery off just as it begins.

长江里的"四大家鱼"为什么特别需要禁渔来保护？

Why do the Yangtze's "four major carps" especially need the fishing ban?

青、草、鲢、鳙是长江流域的旗舰经济鱼，也是很多水鸟的饵料基础；它们产卵依赖特定流水环境，过度捕捞让种群难以补充，禁渔给它们喘息空间。
The black, grass, silver and bighead carps are key economic fish and prey base; they need specific flowing-water spawning grounds, and overfishing left no replenishment—the ban gives them room to recover.
